edges.description: Loss of CSF1R tyrosine kinase signaling directly impairs microglial trophic survival and proliferation, causing progressive microglial depletion, dystrophic morphology, and accumulation of lipid- and iron-laden pigmented glia.

Reduced CSF-1R signaling disrupts the homeostatic balance between CSF-1R and CSF-2R signaling in microglia, driving compensatory upregulation of cerebral CSF-2 (GM-CSF) transcripts and downstream CSF-2 target genes.

Loss of homeostatic microglial trophic support and clearance function triggers neuroaxonal transport failure, axonal swelling, and accumulation of neurofilament- and APP-positive axonal spheroids in cerebral white matter.
edges.target: Primary Axonal Degeneration and Spheroid Formation

edges.description: Microglial depletion and dyshomeostasis induce pro-inflammatory chemokine release (CCL2/MCP-1) and reactive GFAP-positive astrogliosis in cerebral white matter.
Loss of homeostatic microglial clearance of calcium phosphate precipitates leads to dystrophic calcification in periventricular white matter.
Elevated cerebral CSF-2 signaling drives maladaptive microglial activation and transcriptomic programs of oxidative stress.
Unbalanced CSF-2 signaling in CSF1R-deficient microglia promotes demyelination-associated transcriptomic and histopathological changes in cerebral white matter.

nodes.description: CSF1R encodes the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor, a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed predominantly on microglia. Disease-causing variants cluster in the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain and abolish CSF-1-stimulated receptor autophosphorylation, producing loss of kinase activity via haploinsufficiency or dominant-negative inhibition of wild-type receptor dimers. Because CSF1R is the primary regulator of microglial proliferation, survival, and differentiation, impaired CSF1R signaling initiates a primary microgliopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the colony stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) gene cause hereditary diffuse leukoencephalopathy with spheroids.
evidence.snippet: As CSF1R is a crucial mediator of microglial proliferation and differentiation in the brain, our findings suggest an important role for microglial dysfunction in HDLS pathogenesis.

nodes.description: Impaired CSF1R signaling causes a primary microgliopathy characterized by loss of homeostatic P2RY12-positive microglia, regional microglial attrition in subcortical white matter, and transformation of surviving microglia into dystrophic, CD68/CD163-positive, PAS- and iron-positive pigmented glia containing lipofuscin and ceroid bodies. nodes.description: An emerging, preclinical microglia-replacement strategy. Transplantation of human iPSC-derived microglial (iMG) progenitors into a microglia-deficient (Csf1r FIRE-enhancer-deleted) ALSP mouse model restores a homeostatic microglial signature and prevents axonal spheroids, white-matter abnormalities, reactive astrocytosis, and brain calcifications. CRISPR-corrected ALSP-patient-derived iMG can reverse pre-existing pathology, supporting iMG transplantation as a candidate disease-modifying therapy. Not yet in human use.
